# **Problem statement**

## **Stakeholders**

- *Me myself & I*

## **Summary**

At ThirdEye, we want to release our first MVP product, Scout. Scout will serve as an AI order function. The procurement AI assistant serves wholesale/reseller distributors. This will save operators data entry errors, save them time on routine status checks, and catch buyer/seller discrepancies. In this Tech Spec we will address its home card (Supplier list) and 3 features: Otto, Check-up, and Audit 

## **Goals**

Broad

- Get a better understanding of how feature work together
- Brainstorm different implementations/techniques of each of these features
- Figure out scope & magnitude of engineering requirement for each feature
    - Then use this to prioritize the order implementation of each
    - Also just figure out how much of these features are possible

Specific

- Correctly capture and interpret client & Supplier conversations for all feature operations
    - Not only capture a conversation but be able to access it in history
- Easily connect & integrate external ERPs at onboarding phase
    - Start with 1 ERP
- Have user in the loop confirmation of Otto-Mode ERP entry
- Correctly integrate Email sending with Checkups
- Accurately capture Audit Findings

## **Non-goals**

- *Add in many microservices or unneeded complexity*
- *Get stalled by complex issues*
- *Optimize solutions instead of just sticking with first 1-2 solutions*
- *Configure accounts first & create entire Overseer layout*

# Initial Questions:

Answers

- [All] How do we get access to real-time email data, that is in-box and history?
    - Is there an Outlook API? Is there an option for Add-ins to get data to your personal email?
- **Office.js (the add-in runtime)** gives you the *currently open item*. When a user opens Maria's email, Office.context.mailbox.item hands you the subject, body, sender, recipients, attachments, and conversation ID directly. This is how Otto-Mode reads "the open email" — no API call needed, it's right there in the add-in context. This is synchronous-ish and free
- **Microsoft Graph API** gives you everything else — the full mailbox, history, threads, folders, sending, scheduling. This is a REST API (https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages) that your Overseer backend calls with an OAuth token. For "inbox and history," Graph is what you want: you can list messages, filter by conversation, read full thread history, etc.
- **The auth flow** is the important architectural piece: the add-in (Loki) uses Office.auth.getAccessToken() (SSO) or MSAL to get a token scoped to Microsoft Graph, hands it to Overseer, and Overseer calls Graph on the user's behalf. For "personal email" specifically — yes, add-ins work with personal Microsoft accounts (outlook.com) as well as work/school accounts, though some Graph features and admin consent flows differ between them.
- **For real-time** (e.g., the Audit feature monitoring threads "live"), you don't poll Graph constantly. You use **Graph change notifications (webhooks/subscriptions)** — you subscribe to a mailbox folder, and Microsoft POSTs to your Overseer endpoint when new mail arrives. This is exactly the webhook-handling case we discussed: accept the notification, enqueue, return 200 fast.
- [All] How do we scrape message “text” from emails for descriptions on certain Cards?

This is straightforward — the body comes from either source above. item.body.getAsync() in Office.js gives you the open email's body (HTML or plain text); Graph's message object has body and bodyPreview fields. The "scraping" you're really asking about is *extraction* — pulling "ship date: Jul 2" and "$42.50/unit" out of prose. That's not an email-API problem, it's an LLM/NLP problem: you feed the body text to a model and ask for structured fields. That's your AI inference component, and it's the heart of Otto-Mode and Audit.

- [All] how do we scrape contact email information or company names of emails from the conversations or email

Sender address and display name come free with every message (item.from, or Graph's from.emailAddress.address / .name). Company name is trickier — it's usually *inferred*, not given. You have a few options: parse the email domain (@acmesteel.com → "Acme Steel"), use Graph's /me/contacts or the organization's directory, or have your LLM infer it from signature blocks. For an MVP, domain parsing + signature inference covers most cases.

- [All] How do we make sense out of conversations, and create the conversation?
    - Do we have to build the conversation or is there an API for this?

**You don't build threading yourself — the platform gives it to you.** Both Outlook and Graph expose a conversationId on every message. Graph lets you query all messages in a conversation, so the thread is assembled for you. What you *do* build is the *interpretation* — turning 14 messages into "price changed $41 → $42.50." Again, that's LLM work: fetch the thread via Graph, pass it to your inference layer, get back structured findings. So: thread *assembly* = Graph API (free), thread *understanding* = your AI component.

- [Check-ups] How can we schedule emails to be sent based off submission into BE
    - What external services can we use to trigger this? Do we store this in DB, then to Sendgrid at time of Execution? Or just to a service like Send-Grid that stores this? How much do these external services cost?

That changes the scheduling answer: **store the schedule in your own DB (in Overseer), run a scheduler/worker that wakes up at execution time, and call Graph to send.** You don't need an external scheduling service for an MVP — a job table plus a cron-like worker (or a lightweight scheduler) inside Overseer is enough. This is the same async/worker pattern from before.

- [Otto] How do we locate specific resources on ERP through the extension for Otto-Feature?
    - Example: Targeting a specific transaction on QuickBook resource or the Inventory resource Tab in Quickbooks

For an MVP, a real suggestion: **start with one ERP, and consider starting with the "Excel / Sheets" option your prototype already offers.** A spreadsheet write is dramatically simpler than NetSuite's API surface, lets you validate the whole Otto extract-confirm-record loop end to end, and defers the genuinely heavy ERP-integration work until you've proven the core flow.

# **Proposed Solution**

### Reminders when Designing:

- Naming: you want to name for functionality & note for specific feature since there may be changes
- Design so that these endpoints are also compatible with as many UI interface Clients as possible such as a self-hosted Web-App dashboard - in this specific case

### API Conventions (applies to everything below)

- **REST, resource-oriented URLs, no verbs in paths**: `GET /orders`, `POST /checkups`, `PATCH /checkups/{id}`. The HTTP method is the verb. This is what keeps the API reusable by the add-in, a web dashboard, or any future client.
- **Layering rule (never break this)**: `controller / worker → usecase → gateway / repo`. Controllers are HTTP entrypoints only. Usecases never call controllers. Workers (scheduler, webhook jobs) call usecases directly.
- **One realtime channel, not one endpoint per event**: a single `GET /ws` (or SSE `/events`) connection that pushes typed events: `{ "type": "order.updated" | "discrepancy.found", "data": {...} }`. Every client connects once and switches on `type`. New features add event types, not new sockets.
- **Server generates IDs**: clients never send `CheckupID`/`FlowID` etc. on create; the server mints them and returns them in the response.
- **Long work is async**: anything that fans out to Graph + LLM (initial sync, Otto scan) returns fast with an id, and delivers results via the realtime channel or a follow-up GET.
- **Casing**: pick one per layer and stick to it — `camelCase` for JSON fields, `snake_case` for DB columns, `PascalCase` for Go types. (The doc currently mixes `GetActiveOrderList`, `send_due_checkups`, `findExcelResources`.)

# LLM Gateway (shared)

Every feature below has an LLM step — filtering, extraction, ranking, discrepancy detection. The LLM is an external service exactly like Graph, so it gets a gateway: **usecases never call a model/provider directly**.

### `gateway/llm` (BE->LLM provider)

One gateway, task-shaped methods — usecases ask for *outcomes*, not completions. Prompts, model choice, retries, timeouts, structured-output validation, and token/cost logging all live inside this gateway, so swapping the model is a one-file change:

```go
type LLMGateway interface {
	FilterOrderMessages(messages)        // sync: keep only order-related threads — BuildActiveOrderList
	ExtractOrderFields(thread)           // structured fields from a thread — sync, HandleChangeMessage, Otto scan
	RankDestinations(fields, candidates) // Otto: pick top-3 sheets from drive search results
	PlanSheetAppend(structure, fields)   // Otto RecordOrder: where/how to append — never re-decides values
	FindDiscrepancies(newMsg, history)   // Audit
}
```

- **The usecase is the agent loop.** No "Master Agent" gateway that calls other gateways — a gateway that calls gateways is an agent, not an adapter. Orchestration (call llm → call drive search → feed results back to llm) belongs in the usecase, where every step is loggable and debuggable. Each `gateway/llm` method is exactly one model call.
- Validate model output at the gateway boundary (valid JSON, dates parse, enums match) and retry there — usecases only ever see clean structs or an error.
- Cost logging from day one: the initial sync alone pushes a month of messages through this gateway.

## First Phase (Sync)

- This will sync with Inbox to get initial supplier data
- This only occurs once on user onboarding
- Split into two endpoints — a GET must never trigger a sync (it's slow and not idempotent):
    - `POST controller/sync` — called once at onboarding. Kicks off the Graph fetch + LLM formatting as an **async job** (a month of messages through an LLM can take minutes; don't hold the HTTP request open). Returns `202 { syncId }`; completion is pushed over the realtime channel.
    - `GET controller/orders` — read-only, returns whatever is in the `orders` table. Supports `?status=active&cursor=...&limit=...` so any UI can filter/paginate.

### `GET controller/orders` (FE->BE)

```sql
{ 

orders: [ {

CompanyName: “Delmar Tooling”, // string

OrderID: 4471, // int

DateCreated: Date.date // Either send this through or get Auth Context

Status: In Transit, // Status Enum

OriginalEstDate: Date.date, // date type

CurrentEstDate: Date.date, // date type

LastMessenger: User, // userType

Supporting Quote: “Following up on the bracket quote", / string

} , ... ],

nextCursor: "..." // opaque pagination cursor, null when no more pages

}
```

### `usecase/orders/BuildActiveOrderList`

- Calls Graph Gateway to get Message data
- Calls `gateway/llm.FilterOrderMessages` to drop non-order threads, then `gateway/llm.ExtractOrderFields` for formatting
- Upsert into `orders` db as a row
- returns `orders`

### `usecase/orders/FormatInitialOrderData`

- Sends Message Payload to `gateway/llm` for filtering & formatting (was "External Agent" — the model sits behind the gateway, never called raw from a usecase)
    - Only messages with orders are kept
- Return the Response with the desired JSON format which is on the controller

### `gateway/graph/ListMessages` (BE->MSFT Graph)

- Methods to use: list_messages
- Gets all messages/conversations from last month

# Second Phase (Post-Sync)

### Basic Change Notification for Messages

{HTTP method} https://graph.microsoft.com/{version}/{resource}?{query-parameters}

- Use **message** resource type returning `message_id`
- `POST controller/webhooks/graph` — the endpoint Graph POSTs notifications to. Two must-dos:
    - On subscription creation Graph sends a `validationToken` — echo it back with 200 within 10 seconds or the subscription fails
    - On real notifications: enqueue the job and return 202 immediately — never do Graph/LLM work inside the webhook handler
- Message subscriptions **expire (~3 days max)** — needs a small renewal job (the scheduler worker below can own this too)
- Graph can deliver the same notification more than once — `jobs/HandleChangeMessage` must be idempotent (upsert keyed on message id)

## `jobs/HandleChangeMessage`

*Note: Break Below apart*

- Receives notification for change notification getting message ID
- Calls Gateway GET using messageID to get latest message
- Calls `gateway/llm.ExtractOrderFields` to structure the message
- Upserts & updates the DB
    - DB upsert trigger
- Send to FE as an `order.updated` event over the shared realtime channel
- **Also owns reply detection**: if the message is a reply on a conversation that has pending checkup messages with `CancelIfReply`, cancel them here — this is the only place in the system that sees replies, and nothing else wires Checkups' `CancelIfReply` flag to reality

### `gateway/graph/GetMessage`

- Gateway to receive a specific message (lives beside `gateway/graph/ListMessages` — all Graph calls under one gateway namespace)

### `usecase/messages/GetLatestMessage`

- Use `message{id}` to get the latest message (a usecase gets a function-style name — URL-shaped names belong to controllers/gateways only)

### **Params Needed** :

- `createdDateTime`
- `from`
- `Subject`
- `Body`:
- `conversationid`: The ID of the conversation the email belongs to.
- `conversationIndex` (The ID of the conversation the email belongs to.)
- `Id` (Unique identifier for the message.)

- One realtime connection for the whole app; this is one event **type** on it (Audit's `discrepancy.found` is another). Don't create a websocket endpoint per feature — this doc previously defined `controller/Websocket/UpdatedMessage` twice with two different payloads.
- Event payload (`data`):

```sql
{ 
	CompanyName: “Delmar Tooling”, // string

	OrderID: 4471, // int

	DateCreated: Date.date // Either send this through or get Auth Context

	Status: In Transit, // Status Enum

	OriginalEstDate: Date.date, // date type

	CurrentEstDate: Date.date, // date type

	LastMessenger: User, // userType

	Supporting Quote: “Following up on the bracket quote", // string

}
```

- Should trigger request when outlook gets a new email in active session
- On reload, should load all new emails as well

# Otto

### Live

Initial Thoughts: 

- Starting with ___ integrations: Begin with Excel first
    - MSFT graph API supports writing into Execl Files: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/excel-write-to-workbook

- Flow:
    - User hovers over new email → Parses information → Send to LLM to locate Excel Files to locate files/folder in background → confirms details to submit (editing info. card phase) → Pick ERP Card (Excel in our case) → Show related Sheets that it found, which user selects → Writes in the recording in the same structure that it was previously being recorded in → returns link for user to proof read and check and order detail
- Revised Flow:
    - User opens email → clicks Ask Otto
    → FE sends { messageId, conversationId }
    → BE: fetch thread (Graph) → LLM extract fields
    → BE: resolve destination — mapping lookup; cold start → drive search → user picks → save
    → FE: ONE confirm card: editable fields + destination shown ("Orders 2026.xlsx → PO_Log") + change link
    → approve (confirmationId) → RecordOrder → append table row → return webUrl
    → card: "Recorded ✓ — open sheet"

Note: you will need to ask user to allow permissions into Excel File/One-drive

What data needs to be sent from FE to BE when an email is being Scanned?

- `conversationId`
    - You want to be able to have the whole context history of the conversation so you can get an idea of where the resource is located & what params to get
- `message_id`
    - You want to be able to locate this message

Actions that use-cases should handle: 

- Parsing out information from new message
- Accepting Edits from User
- Linking new message to previous conversation
- Finding the related resource/sheet for Excel Files using the conversation Information
    - Requires to look up previous conversation context and new information
- Filling in the resource with the updated information

### `POST controller/otto/scans`

```python
{
  "messageId":      "<REST id>",
  "conversationId": "<id>"
}
```

- `userId` comes from the auth token — never from the request body (a client that can set its own userId can read other users' data)
- Response: `{ scanId, extractedFields, destinations: [top 3] }` — the FE renders the confirm card directly from this
- This call fans out to Graph + LLM; if it runs long in practice, return `scanId` immediately (202) and push the results as an event over the realtime channel

### `usecase/otto/ResolveDestinations`

*(renamed from `findExcelResources` — per the naming reminder above, name for functionality, not for the current integration; the same usecase will later resolve QuickBooks/NetSuite destinations)*

- Receives payload from `controller/otto/scans` then gets calls on gateway to get latest message and full conversation using id’s in payload
    - [Q]: Do I use my previous calls for this — yes: reuse `gateway/graph/ListMessages` / `GetLatestMessage`, don't duplicate Graph calls per feature
    - Calls on DB query to store the scan into the `otto_scans` table (one name — this doc previously called it `Otto_Scans`, `otto_email_scans`, and `otto_scan`)
- **This usecase is the agent loop** (was Master LLM Agent + sub-agent — a gateway that calls other gateways is an agent, not an adapter; the orchestration lives here instead, where each step is loggable). Three plain gateway calls in sequence:
    1. `gateway/llm.ExtractOrderFields(conversation)` — structured fields (Supplier, Company, order), emphasizing the most recent message
    2. `gateway/drive_gateway` — run the search queries below using those fields to find matching resources
    3. `gateway/llm.RankDestinations(fields, searchResults)` — selects the sheets/resources most aligned with the conversation & latest message
- Returns top 3 recommended resources with their link address

### `gateway/drive_gateway` (search) + `gateway/excel_gateway` (write)

Two gateways, not one: the searches below are **OneDrive** calls (`/me/drive/...`), so they live in `drive_gateway`. `excel_gateway` is the write side — the workbook table-row append used by `RecordOrder`.

Uses recent message fields to query for worksheets 

- GET /me/drive/search(q='{supplierName}')      ← "Delmar" — files named after the vendor
GET /me/drive/search(q='{poNumber}')          ← "4471" — hits file *content* too
GET /me/drive/search(q='orders')              ← generic log names
GET /me/drive/search(q='PO')
GET /me/drive/recent                          ← no query at all — see below

### `POST controller/otto/scans/{scanId}/record`

*(renamed from `SendSelectedResource` — this call is the **human-in-the-loop approval** from the Goals section: nothing is ever written to the ERP until it happens)*

```python
{
	"selectedResource": "<drive item id / URL>",  # string — the destination the user picked
	"fields": { ... }                             # the user-EDITED fields from the confirm card
}
```

- `scanId` in the path locates the stored scan — no need to resend MessageID
- `fields` must be what the user approved on the card, not the raw LLM extraction — otherwise the confirm step is theater

### `usecase/otto/RecordOrder`

- Queries `otto_scans` using `scanId`
- Calls `gateway/llm.PlanSheetAppend(workbook structure, user-approved fields)`
    - LLM observes Excel File structure (columns / existing table)
    - Decides only *where/how* to append — it does **not** re-decide the values; the user already approved those
- Appends the row via `gateway/excel_gateway` (the usecase writes; the LLM only plans)
- Marks the scan `recorded` and returns the sheet `webUrl` for the "Recorded ✓ — open sheet" card

Initial Thoughts

- Will need DB of Check-ups to immediately populated them on refresh on the List
- Add Check up → Step Selection
    - Step Selection has Vendor Selected, Email Selected Cadence, Only if No reply, Repeat every XYZ, Stop after _
- What are the benefits of adding in Check-ups?

- **For DB, every row should be a message and not a Flow**

Design Questions:

- Do we want to have the option to create all checkup messages, when creating a checkup?
- What type of messaging logic, do we want?
    - Cancel the message if there is a reply?

### Create a Checkup

### `gateway/graph/SendMail`

*(was `POST controller/Websocket/SendMessage` — but nothing external calls this and no websocket is involved. It's a gateway the scheduler-driven usecase calls. A usecase must never call a controller — that inverts the layering.)*

- Calls Graph `POST /me/sendMail` to create & send the message
- The **usecase** (not the gateway) marks the row `sent` after the send succeeds — gateways talk to external services, they don't touch our DB

### `usecase/checkups/SendDueCheckups`

- Trigger by scheduler
- Queries checkups that are due: `SendDate <= now AND Status = 'pending'` — **not** `== now`; the ticker will never land exactly on SendDate, an equality check silently sends nothing
- Calls `gateway/graph/SendMail` for each due message
- Marks each row `sent` — claim the row first (e.g. `UPDATE ... SET status='sending' WHERE status='pending'` or `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`) so two worker instances can't double-send the same email

### `workers/scheduler`

- **Start a ticker** — `time.NewTicker(time.Minute)` fires a signal onto a channel every 60 seconds.
- **Loop forever, waiting** on two things at once: the tick, or a shutdown signal.
- **On each tick, call `uc.Execute(ctx)`** — that's the entire hand-off. It doesn't know what a checkup is, doesn't touch the DB, doesn't know Graph exists. It just says "it's time, go" and the use case does everything.
- **Log the error if `Execute` fails** — and crucially, *keep looping*. One bad tick must not kill the scheduler; the next minute it tries again.
- **Exit cleanly on `ctx.Done()`** — when you deploy or Ctrl-C the app, the context is cancelled, the loop returns, no ticks fire mid-shutdown.

### `usecase/checkups/CreateCheckupMessages`

- Receives payload from CreateCheckup
- Computes SendTime of each message according to the Payloads Cadence
- Upserts each message into the Checkups Table
    - Table should have `Status` of Message, `SendTime` , `Cancelled`

### `POST controller/checkups`

```python
{
	# CheckupID / FlowID removed — the server generates IDs and returns them in the response; clients never mint IDs
	CompanyName: “Delmar Tooling”, # string
	EmailAddress: "johndo@gmmail.com"
	OrderID: 4471, # int
	DateCreated: Date.date # Either send this through or get Auth Context
	Subject: string
	Body: string
	SendDate: time.Time // This will be the time the message is sent at
	CurrentEstDate: Date.date, // date type
	CancelIfReply: Bool
	RepeatFlow: Int 

}
```

### Toggling on/off

### `usecase/checkups/UpdateStatus`

- Updates `Status` field of Checkup Message in DB Table using CheckupID
- **One status enum, used everywhere** (this doc previously had three vocabularies: pending/cancelled/sent, "Paused", and "sent-cancelled-awaiting" in the schema):
    - `pending` — scheduled, will send
    - `paused` — toggle off; resumable back to `pending`
    - `sent` — terminal, set by the sender
    - `cancelled` — terminal (user cancelled, or `CancelIfReply` fired)

### `PATCH controller/checkups/{checkupId}`

*(was `POST .../ToggleCheckup` — a partial update to an existing resource is a `PATCH`, with the id in the path. This one endpoint covers pause, resume, and cancel — no separate toggle/cancel endpoints needed.)*

```sql
{
	Status: "paused" // "pending" to resume, "cancelled" to kill

}
```

# **Audit**

### Ideas

Flow Ideas;

- Change Notification -> Check for Discrepancy: LLM compares new message with conversation history, querying DB for the conversation. History -> if a discrepancy is found -> Store in Discrepancies DB for source of truth -> send to FE using Websock
    - The UI is provided with the email address link so they can draft the email. This is provided on our API schema.
- The WebSocket client is only gets the audit notification when a client is connected, so you can make a discrepancies DB Table to then send trigger the DB call once Client is connected

## `usecase/orders/CatchDiscrepancies`

- Triggered by change notification worker
- Queries the table for conversation history for that specific conversation that has the change notification using conversation_id
    - **Gap this doc must close**: there is no messages table, and `Orders` had no `conversation_id` column, so "the table for conversation history" didn't exist. MVP answer: add `conversation_id` to `Orders` (done in Schema Updates below) and **re-fetch the thread from Graph at audit time** — no messages table needed yet, and Graph is the source of truth anyway
- Calls `gateway/llm.FindDiscrepancies(newMessage, history)`; if a discrepancy is found, stores it in the Discrepancies DB
    - As well as discrepancy quotes, email address URLs are also kept
- Send that specific discrepancy to FE using a websocket

## Realtime event: `discrepancy.found` (BE->FE over the shared `GET /ws`)

*(was a second `controller/Websocket/UpdatedMessage` — same name as the order-update endpoint but a different payload. It's the same socket; this is just a second event type on it.)*

- *Think about what data you want shown on the frontend*

```python
{
	CompanyName: “Delmar Tooling”, // string

	Email:

	EmailDeeplinkURL:

	OrderID: 4471, // int

	DateCreated: Date.date // Either send this through or get Auth ContexT

	Priortiy: High // PriorityEnum: High/Med/Low

	Discrepancy Title:

	DiscrepancyDetail: { PreviouslyAgreedOnMetric: New Metric} // types will be Price/Date/Unit.

	DiscrepancyQuotes: String of old Conversation History w/ Link to Message

}
```

**Dependencies**

*Which services you need to rely on for this solution? Are there any other projects that need to be completed first?*

- **Microsoft Graph** (mail read/send, change notifications, OneDrive search, Excel workbook writes) + **Office.js/MSAL** for the add-in auth handoff
- **LLM provider** for extraction/formatting/discrepancy detection — always behind `gateway/llm` (see LLM Gateway section)
- **Must exist before any feature works** (currently unwritten in this doc):
    - Auth/onboarding flow: exchange the add-in SSO token, store the Graph **refresh token** per user (encrypted), create the mailbox subscription. The backing tables (`accounts`, `users`, `graph_subscriptions`) are defined in Schema Updates below
    - The shared realtime channel (`GET /ws` or SSE) that Order List, Otto, and Audit all push events through
- Build order that de-risks fastest: **auth + sync + `GET /orders`** → **webhook + `order.updated`** (proves the realtime spine) → **Otto** (reuses both) → **Checkups** (adds scheduler) → **Audit** (pure add-on to the webhook job)

## **Schema Updates**

Conventions: Postgres, `snake_case` columns. Every table carries **`account_id`** (the company/tenant — the distributor org) and **`user_id`** (the individual operator whose mailbox the data came from) — these are how every query locates the user who owns these orders, and every controller filters on them from auth context. The old `Base` shorthand is spelled out as real columns (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`).

MVP note: seed one account + one user row (single-user mode) — the columns exist now so multi-user later is a login page, not a migration.

Accounts & Users (the FK targets — the "must exist first" tables from Dependencies)

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (
    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    company_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id                      UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    account_id              UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    email                   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    graph_refresh_token_enc TEXT,                             -- encrypted at rest; the plumbing every feature depends on
    created_at              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS graph_subscriptions (
    id                    UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id               UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    graph_subscription_id TEXT NOT NULL,                      -- Microsoft's id for the webhook subscription
    expires_at            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,                -- renewal job reads this (~3-day max lifetime)
    created_at            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

Orders

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS orders (
    id                UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    account_id        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    user_id           UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),     -- whose mailbox this order came from
    conversation_id   TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- Graph conversation id — HandleChangeMessage and Audit look rows up by this
    company_name      TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- "Delmar Tooling"
    email_address     TEXT,
    order_id          INTEGER,                                -- supplier's PO number (business identifier), NOT the row PK; switch to TEXT if suppliers use alphanumeric POs
    email_url         TEXT,
    status            TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- Status Enum, e.g. 'in_transit'
    original_est_date DATE,
    current_est_date  DATE,
    last_messenger    TEXT,
    supporting_quote  TEXT,                                   -- "Following up on the bracket quote"
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_conversation ON orders (user_id, conversation_id); -- the webhook-job lookup path
```

Discrepancies

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS discrepancies (
    id                 UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    account_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    user_id            UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    conversation_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
    status             TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open','resolved','dismissed')), -- the UI needs to clear findings, not show them forever
    company_name       TEXT NOT NULL,
    email_address      TEXT,
    email_deeplink_url TEXT,                                  -- so the UI can open a draft to the supplier
    order_id           INTEGER,
    priority           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (priority IN ('high','medium','low')),
    discrepancy_title  TEXT NOT NULL,
    discrepancy_detail JSONB,                                 -- { "previously_agreed": ..., "new_metric": ..., "type": "price" | "date" | "unit" }
    discrepancy_quotes JSONB,                                 -- [{ "quote": ..., "message_link": ... }] — old conversation history w/ link to message
    created_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```

Checkup Messages

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS checkup_messages (                 -- one row per scheduled MESSAGE, not per flow
    id               UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- this IS the CheckupID that PATCH /checkups/{checkupId} targets — no separate column
    account_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    user_id          UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    flow_id          UUID NOT NULL,                           -- groups the messages minted together by one POST /checkups
    conversation_id  TEXT,                                    -- lets HandleChangeMessage find pending rows to cancel on reply
    company_name     TEXT NOT NULL,
    email_address    TEXT NOT NULL,
    order_id         INTEGER,
    status           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','paused','sent','cancelled')), -- same enum as usecase/checkups/UpdateStatus
    subject          TEXT NOT NULL,
    body             TEXT NOT NULL,
    send_date        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,                    -- when the message goes out; scheduler queries send_date <= now
    current_est_date DATE,
    cancel_if_reply  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    repeat_flow      INTEGER,
    created_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_checkups_due ON checkup_messages (send_date) WHERE status = 'pending'; -- the scheduler's due query
```

Otto Scans

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS otto_scans (
    id                UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- this is the scanId the controllers use
    account_id        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id),
    user_id           UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    message_id        TEXT NOT NULL,                          -- Graph message id
    conversation_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
    company_name      TEXT,
    email_address     TEXT,
    order_id          INTEGER,
    email_url         TEXT,
    extracted_fields  JSONB,                                  -- what the LLM pulled out — the confirm card edits these; RecordOrder writes the approved version
    selected_resource TEXT,                                   -- set at record time
    status            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'scanned' CHECK (status IN ('scanned','recorded','abandoned')),
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
```
